subject: Dedicated capacity: fallback policy & SLA exception request
messages:
From: Alexandra Park <alexandra@brightgrid.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: observed latency spikes and throughput shortfall

Hi Jonas / Laura,

We started our dedicated pool rollout last week and are seeing intermittent latency spikes during steady traffic — p95 is fine but p99s jump and sustained token throughput is below the committed numbers. This is impacting our inference-heavy feature in production (concurrent inference volume ~ 1.2k requests/min).

Can you confirm:
- How Redwood measures "sustained throughput" for Dedicated pools (tokens/min vs tokens/sec burst smoothing)?
- What fallback behavior you recommend if queued requests start to back up (e.g., model fallback, cross-region routing)?
- Whether an SLA exception or remediation plan is possible while we finish our traffic shaping changes.

We have basic telemetry to share. Attaching a summary of recent p99 spikes and sample traces.

Thanks,
Alexandra Park
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightGrid AI
alexandra@brightgrid.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: observed latency spikes and throughput shortfall

Hi Alexandra — thanks for the notes and the traces.

Short answer: we can provision an SLA exception and a temporary fallback policy while you complete the traffic shaping work, but I need two things from you to scope it properly:
1) Your target sustained throughput (tokens/min) that we should guarantee for the exception window.
2) Your acceptable p99 latency threshold during the exception (we can offer latency tiers tied to credits).

Proposed immediate actions:
- I can open an SLA exception request for a 30-day window and include a cross-region failover option.
- We’ll enable a model-variant fallback (to a lightly-quantized variant) if queue depth exceeds the configured threshold for >60s.
- We’ll run a brief dedicated-pool stress test to verify the queueing behavior; please share peak sustained traffic window.

I’ve attached the SLA exception form for signoff (internal and legal need this to track deviation). Please fill the top section and return; I’ll loop in our infra ops to set the threshold.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Proposed thresholds and credits for BrightGrid exception

Jonas / Marissa — internal note before we send the formal proposal to BrightGrid.

Context: BrightGrid wants a temporary commitment while they finish shaping. Their traffic profile: sustained windows ~50k tokens/min for 6–8 minute bursts. Observed p99 spikes to 1.2–1.6s during high concurrency.

Suggested SLA exception terms (draft):
- Duration: 30 days from signoff; auto-review at day 14.
- Throughput guarantee: sustained 50,000 tokens/min with 60s smoothing window.
- Latency tier: p99 < 250ms; if p99 > 250ms for >5 minutes, auto-trigger: enable model-variant fallback + cross-region spillover.
- Credits: If sustained throughput falls below 95% of guarantee for >10m, apply credit equal to 5% of that month’s Dedicated commit prorated.
- Escalation: Primary ops contact ops@redwood.ai, secondary: infra@redwood.ai, internal on-call notified.

Attached is the June benchmark we ran against similar pools — use the numbers for justification when we present.

Laura
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[attachment: throughput_benchmark_2026-06.csv]

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: fallback policy & SLA exception request

Thanks — that looks promising. A few clarifications before we sign the exception form:

- Our minimum acceptable sustained throughput for the exception window is 50,000 tokens/min (matches Laura's proposal).
- For latency, our product owners require p99 <= 250ms for critical endpoints; if you can commit to the 250ms p99 target with the stated fallback policy, we can proceed.
- Please include explicit escalation contacts (email + phone) and an agreed test plan to validate the cross-region spillover behavior before the exception goes live.

If those are included in the exception doc, procurement will expedite. Can you also confirm whether the cross-region spillover will incur additional egress or capacity charges during the remediation window?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
Alexandra Park
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightGrid AI
alexandra@brightgrid.ai

Alex — great, thanks for the clear targets.

We’ll include the following in the formal exception package and DocuSign agreement:
- Throughput guarantee: 50,000 tokens/min (60s smoothing).
- Latency guarantee: p99 <= 250ms; fallback to model-variant + cross-region spillover if p99 > 250ms for >5m.
- Escalation contacts: ops@redwood.ai (primary ops inbox, monitored 08:00–20:00 PT), +1-415-555-0132 (on-call escalation). Secondary: infra@redwood.ai.
- Cost: cross-region spillover will only be enabled as part of the remediation policy and will not trigger additional egress charges for the exception window; any sustained usage beyond the 30-day exception will be billed per standard committed-capacity terms.
- Test plan: ops will run a controlled failover test with BrightGrid during the first 72 hours post-signoff; we’ll schedule a 60-minute runbook review beforehand.

Next steps: I’ll populate the SLA_exception_form.pdf with these terms and send the DocuSign link (see HubSpot/Deal link). Once signed, ops will schedule the verification test.
